Fit an outcome model on the matched population

Source: R/OutcomeModels.R
fitOutcomeModel.Rd

Fits a regression model for the outcome using Cyclops. By default, a stratified Cox proportional-hazards model stratified by `stratumId` (matched set) is used, which is the standard analysis for the prevalent new-user design.

Usage

fitOutcomeModel(population, pnuData = NULL, outcomeModelArgs)

Arguments

population

A data frame from [matchOnTcps()] containing `row_id`, `treatment`, `stratumId`, `survival_time`, and `outcome_count`.

pnuData

A [PnuData] object. Required when `useCovariates = TRUE` (for `covariates` and `covariateRef` tables).

outcomeModelArgs

An `OutcomeModelArgs` object from [createOutcomeModelArgs()].

Value

A named list of class `"OutcomeModel"` with elements:

`logRr`

Log hazard (or odds / rate) ratio for the treatment.

`seLogRr`

Standard error of `logRr`, derived from the profile CI.

`p`

Two-sided p-value.

`ci95Lb`

Lower bound of the 95% confidence interval on the ratio scale.

`ci95Ub`

Upper bound of the 95% confidence interval on the ratio scale.

`status`

`"OK"` or a description of why the model could not be fit.

`outcomeModelType`

Value of `modelType`.

`outcomeModelStratified`

Value of `stratified`.

Details

Only strata with at least one outcome event contribute to the stratified model likelihood. Strata with zero events are dropped before fitting (standard partial-likelihood behaviour).

The treatment estimate is the coefficient for the binary `treatment` covariate. When `useCovariates = FALSE` (default), no other covariates are included and no regularization is applied (`prior = "none"`). When `useCovariates = TRUE`, all covariates from `pnuData$covariates` are included as additional adjusters; the treatment coefficient remains unpenalised.

References

Suissa S, Moodie EE, Dell'Aniello S. Prevalent new-user cohort designs for comparative drug effect studies by time-conditional propensity scores. *Pharmacoepidemiol Drug Saf* 2017;26(4):459-468. doi:10.1002/pds.4117

See also

[createOutcomeModelArgs()], [matchOnTcps()]

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
simArgs <- createSimulationArgs(
  nSwitchers = 500L, nCovariates = 0L,
  logRr = log(2), seed = 1L
)
pnuData <- simulatePnuData(simArgs)
pnuData <- createStudyPopulation(pnuData, createStudyPopulationArgs(outcomeId = 1L))
pop <- dplyr::collect(pnuData$studyPopulation)
pop$propensityScore <- 0.5
matched <- matchOnTcps(pop, createMatchingArgs())
result <- fitOutcomeModel(matched, pnuData, createOutcomeModelArgs())
Andromeda::close(pnuData)
} # }
